# A Gantt's links paint over its locked columns after a horizontal scroll

## Context

Found reading #21626's scrolled 1440 × 900 frame (`gantt/taskColumns`): after a horizontal scroll, links whose bars have left the chart are drawn across the locked table, through Owner, Start and Done.

It is already on `dev` `4b444e4e7a`, in the released examples. Instrument: two screenshots of the locked columns' area, one with `.neo-gantt-dependency-layer` shown and one with it at `visibility: hidden`; a second shown frame proves the page stable. 1440 × 900, `neo-theme-neo-dark`:

| Example | Horizontal scroll | Locked columns' pixels change when the links hide |
|---|---|---|
| `gantt/zoom` | 0, 900 | no |
| `gantt/zoom` | 2400 | **yes** |
| `gantt/basic` | 0, 600 | no |
| `gantt/basic` | 300 | **yes** |

A hit test cannot see it: the layer has `pointer-events: none`, so `elementFromPoint` returns the cell either way.

## The Problem

Center cells scroll with `transform: translateX(calc(var(--grid-scroll-left, 0px) * -1))` inside rows with `contain: strict` (`resources/css/src/grid/Body.css`), so every row clips its cells to the region. The dependency layer scrolls with the same transform but sits directly in the center `.neo-grid-body`, which is `overflow-x: visible`. Nothing clips it, so the part of a link left of the visible chart paints over the locked-start body: the layer is `z-index: 4`, and the locked cells' `z-index: 5` stays inside each row's own stacking context.

## The Architectural Reality

- `.neo-gantt-dependency-layer` (`resources/css/src/gantt/Container.css`): `position: absolute`, `overflow: visible`, `pointer-events: none`, `z-index: 4`, translated by `--grid-scroll-left`.
- `Neo.gantt.DependencyLayer` (`src/gantt/DependencyLayer.mjs`) is as wide as the whole axis and projects a buffered window of it.
- `.neo-grid-body` is `overflow-x: visible` for every grid (`resources/css/src/grid/Body.css:3`, since the multi-body architecture, `#9633`).
- Design authority: `Neo.gantt.DependencyLayer` @description: "Renders directed task dependencies (`FS`, `SS`, `FF`, `SF`) inside a single `<svg>` element layered over the center timeline track". Links over the locked columns are outside that track.

## The Fix

In `resources/css/src/gantt/Container.css`, the body that hosts the layer clips horizontally:

```css
.neo-grid-body:has(> .neo-gantt-dependency-layer) {
    overflow-x: clip;
}
```

The clip is static, so a scroll stays a transform of the layer. `overflow-x: clip` leaves `overflow-y` visible. A draft of this rule, on `dev`'s two examples and on `gantt/taskColumns`: the locked columns' pixels no longer change when the links hide, at every scroll above; the chart's pixels still change, so the links still draw.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] In `gantt/zoom` and `gantt/basic` at 1440 × 900, no link paints over the locked columns at any horizontal scroll.
- [ ] The links still draw in the chart at those scrolls.
- [ ] A Playwright e2e spec proves both with the shown/hidden pixel comparison: red on `dev`, green at head.
- [ ] The gantt and scheduler e2e specs stay green.

## Out of Scope

- The axis offset of columns before the timeline in its own region (#21684).
- Overlays other than the dependency layer.

## Avoided Traps

- **A hit test as the instrument.** The layer ignores pointer events; only pixels show it.
- **`overflow-x: clip` on every grid body.** Only the Gantt's center body hosts the layer.
- **A `clip-path` on the layer keyed on `--grid-scroll-left`.** It clips correctly, but repaints an axis-wide SVG on every scroll frame.
